items.titleZh: 奥孔离开哈斯车队：媒体团队给出他们的评判
items.summaryZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔将在2026赛季末离开哈斯一事已成定局，F2积分榜领跑者拉斐尔·卡马拉预计将接替他的席位。
items.originalTitle: Our verdict on Ocon's Haas F1 exit
items.summaryEn: Esteban Ocon's departure from Haas at the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season is now official, with F2 points leader Rafael Camara expected to replace him.
detailZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔将在2026年一级方程式赛季末离开哈斯一事已成定局，F2积分榜领跑者拉斐尔·卡马拉预计将接替他的席位。
但奥孔得到了公平的机会吗？我们的团队给出他们的评判……
他的速度不足以证明续约的合理性
我不会把奥孔列为当前22位F1车手中最差的、因此完全活该失去席位，但他可能排在前15名之外，当身后有严重压力时，这就足以让你的位置变得危险。
我认为这个问题的核心在于，哈斯车队的运作成本仍然低于预算上限，且整体资金不足，因此在奥康身上花的钱，必须用比他过去两个赛季所展现出的更高整体表现水平来证明其合理性。
他偶尔闪现过自己的实力，也有过一些短暂且持续的良好状态，但还不足以把他标榜为明确的车队领袖和标杆——而这正是车队付钱让他扮演的角色。
简而言之，奥利·比尔曼速度太快了，哈斯需要节省资金，而奥康的表现还不够好，也不够稳定，无法同时证明他所拿的薪水以及他似乎在幕后给车队带来的压力是值得的。
一级方程式车队可以接受非常强势的个性，但前提是你必须在赛道上用成绩来支撑你的要求。
当你把这些因素再加上一位法拉利青训车手——拉法·卡马拉，他既有法拉利的支持，又有来自巴西的资金 背景支持——在 TPC 测试（借用旧车进行的测试项目）中凭借纯粹的圈速把哈斯车队彻底比下去，就很容易理解为什么，尽管奥孔相比仍在占据一级方程式席位的其他几位车手可能还有更多可提供的价值，但不幸的是，至少目前他已经走到了路的尽头。
考虑到奥孔很有资格被称为发车阵容中最（甚至是唯一？）正常的一个人，他当初能够进入一级方程式，本身就是一项巨大的超水平成就。
他也比自己获得的评价更好——状态最佳时速度极快，而且是一位非常强悍的比赛车手。奥孔确实风格激进，也有可能做出自毁前程的事（无论在赛道上还是赛道外）。但他属于那种车手：只要在一辆中游赛车上得到争夺好成绩的机会，就完全可以指望他把机会把握到底。
如果奥孔留在发车阵容里，整个阵容会更强。不过，他并不总是拿出自己最好的一面，阿尔派车队以及如今哈斯车队的人们都说，他没有意识到主动权在自己手中。这一点一直拖累着他，并造成了不必要的摩擦。
奥孔几乎可以肯定只是认为自己行事直截了当，而且很可能正是哈斯车队在赛季初告诉他所需要的那个角色。也许这其中有几分道理。也许能真正激发他全部潜力的环境一直与他擦肩而过。
如果他找到了那样的环境，和/或在自己性格的不同侧面之间取得了更好的平衡，那么奥通的F1生涯距离结束可能还有好几年。他确实有足够的实力继续占据一个车手席位更长时间。
他的F1生涯并未达到他进入F1前的履历所预示的高度——连续夺得欧洲F3和GP3冠军，加上梅赛德斯的鼎力支持，本让人期待更多。但他的生涯也谈不上糟糕。
不过考虑到他已经征战了九个多赛季的F1比赛，参加了大约200场大奖赛，奥孔已经拥有了一段相当可观的职业生涯，只是他还没有拿出足够有说服力的表现，让人认定如果这段生涯无法延续到第二个十年就会是一种遗憾。
而即便是让他在F1发车区上待到这么久，也并非一帆风顺：他先是被梅赛德斯青训体系挤了出去，后来又在印度力量车队为了让位给斯特罗尔而被挤走，并因此闲置了一年。这两种情况中，其中一种比另一种要公平得多，但他都凭借自己的努力重新爬了回来。
一位非常优秀的车手，虽然有某些局限，但在F1之外的赛车世界里仍能提供很多价值。
不过，对于自己在F1的生涯以何时、何种方式收尾，他没什么可抱怨的。
我认为，在他效力过的车队里，他已经得到了公平的机会，但从未真正展现出格外出众的实力。他一直很出色，但像许多人一样，出色却不够卓越。
另外再补充一点，他从来都不像是一个有团队精神的车手。我记得他经常和队友发生碰撞。没错，他最近表现好了一些，但也许只是因为他们没有长时间在赛道的同一位置上竞争。
还有一个有趣的地方是，自从他被替换的传闻出现后，他在巴库能够提升自己的表现。在我看来，这说明他是一个并不是每次坐进赛车都愿意全力以赴的车手。
另外，我很高兴看到一支车队愿意给有前途的新秀车手机会；在F1中有太多平庸的老将占着席位。我并不是说目前的车手没有能力留在F1，但这项被誉为赛车运动精英中的精英的赛事，总共只有22个席位。
很可能还有大约50名正在低级别方程式中成长的车手，他们比其中50%的人更出色或更有潜力。
抱歉这个裁决有点跑题，但我非常支持让新人才进入F1，让他们与现有的车手阵容同场竞技，展示他们真正的天赋。
F1可以做的一件事是：允许车队在每个大奖赛带三辆组装好的赛车，毕竟他们本来就会带第三辆车作为备件，只是没有完全组装。如果这样做，他们就可以在所有比赛周末的延长版90分钟第一次自由练习中派出三辆赛车——为了减少某些赛事中的车流，可以规定每个车队在任一时刻只允许两辆赛车在赛道上。
对于冲刺赛周末，冲刺排位赛和冲刺赛恢复为两辆赛车参赛，但需立法规定每支车队必须轮换其现有车手，并至少派出一名参加过大奖赛不超过两次的车手。
两名参赛车手获得的冲刺赛积分只计入车队单独的“冲刺车队总冠军”和“冲刺车手总冠军”，这或许能打开一扇门，找到下一个超级巨星。
然后在周六冲刺赛结束之后，两位常规大奖赛车手会接手进行30分钟的第二阶段自由练习，紧接着就进行大奖赛排位赛，而大奖赛则照常在周日举行。
考虑到奥康的一级方程式生涯最初本身就是一件非常 不太可能的事情，我不会排除他再次拼回一级方程式发车区的可能性。
他只有30岁，而且目前的表现水平，可能比自前队友塞尔希奥·佩雷斯2020年惊人结尾以来任何被解雇的车手都要高。
想想角田裕毅（红牛）、佩雷斯（红牛）、丹尼尔·里卡多（阿尔法·托利）、凯文·马格努森（哈斯）、瓦尔特里·博塔斯和周冠宇（索伯）。他们当中没有任何人的表现能接近奥康在最近几轮比赛中所达到的水平。
因此，奥孔拥有八场比赛的现任车手优势这一强大武器，驾驶着一辆升级后的哈斯赛车，如今这辆车在大多数赛道上看起来都有能力争夺积分。
如果他能够继续交出一些击败贝尔曼的比赛周末，那么他离开F1时将留下一个有力的提醒：如果某支F1车队需要一名有经验的车手，无论是作为替补还是正式车手，他应该是首选。
重返F1不会在2027年发生，但或许这足以让他在2028年的人才市场上保持活跃。
detailEn: Esteban Ocon's exit from Haas at the end of the 2026 Formula 1 season is now official, with F2 points leader Rafael Camara expected to replace him.
But was Ocon given a fair chance? Our team gives their verdict...
He wasn't fast enough to justify another deal

I wouldn't rank Ocon as the worst of the current 22 F1 drivers, and therefore completely deserving of dropping off the grid, but he's probably outside the top 15 and that's enough to leave you vulnerable when there's serious pressure from underneath.

I think at the crux of this is that Haas still operates below the cost cap and remains underfunded overall, so the money being spent on Ocon needs to be justified by a higher overall level of performance than he's shown over the past two seasons.
There have been flashes of what he's capable of, and some short spurts of sustained good form, but not enough to mark him out as the clear team leader and reference - which is what he's paid to be.

In short, Ollie Bearman has been too fast, Haas needs to save cash, and Ocon hasn't been good enough, consistently enough, to justify both the money he's being paid and the stress it seems he's put the team under behind the scenes.
F1 teams will accept very demanding personalities, but only if you do the job on track to back up your demands.

When you add all that to a Ferrari junior, in Rafa Camara - who brings Ferrari support as well as financial backing from Brazil - simply blowing Haas away with his sheer pace in TPC testing, it's easy to see why, even though Ocon might still have more to offer than several others still occupying F1 seats, he's unfortunately reached the end of the road, for now.
That Ocon even got to F1 in the first place is a huge overachievement considering he has a strong claim to be the most (only?) normal person on the grid.

He is also better than he gets credit for - extremely fast at his best and a very formidable racer. Ocon's aggressive, sure. And capable of being self-defeating (on track and off it). But he is one of those drivers who, if given a chance at a result in a midfield car, can be completely depended on to see it through.

The grid is stronger if Ocon remains on it. He doesn't always put his best foot forward, though, and people at Alpine and now at Haas say he fails to recognise that agency. This is something that has held him back and caused unnecessary friction.

Ocon almost certainly just sees himself as being straightforward, and probably exactly what Haas told him it needed him to be at the start. And maybe there's some truth to that. Maybe the environment that would get the very best out of him has simply eluded him.
If he finds it, and/or achieves a slightly better balance between his own sides, then Ocon's F1 career could still be years from ending. He's certainly good enough to hold down a seat for longer.
This hasn't lived up to what Ocon's pre-F1 package of back-to-back European F3 and GP3 titles plus Mercedes patronage intimated would be possible. Neither has it been terrible

But given he's had nine and a bit F1 racing seasons, around 200 grands prix, Ocon's had a very healthy career already without providing compelling evidence that it would be a travesty if that career didn't stretch into a second decade.

And even getting his time on the F1 grid to that length hasn't been straightforward, given how he was squeezed off the Mercedes ladder and was the one squeezed out of Force India to accommodate Lance Stroll and had a year on the sidelines as a result. One of those situations was a lot more meritocratic than the other, and he clawed his way back from both.
A very good driver, with some limitations, and plenty to offer the rest of the racing world outside F1.
But he can have no complaints about when and how his time in F1 is concluding.
I think he has had a fair crack at it with the teams he has driven for but never really stood out as being exceptional. He's been good but not exceptional as so many are.

Also to add to that he has never seemed like a team player. I remember him colliding frequently with his team-mates. Yes, he has been better lately, but perhaps that's just because they haven’t been on the same part of the track for very long.
It’s also interesting that since these rumours of him being replaced, he was able to up his game in Baku. To me, that shows a driver who is not willing to give his all every time he sits in the car.

Also, I’m very happy to see a team giving up and coming drivers an opportunity; we have far too many journeymen retaining seats in F1. I’m not saying any of the current drivers are not capable of being in F1, but there are only 22 seats in the formula that is classified as the cream de la crème of motorsport.
There are probably 50 other drivers out there coming through the lower formulas that are better or have more potential than 50% of them.
Sorry to go off piste with this verdict, but I am a big fan of getting new talent into F1 to allow them to show their true talent against the resident pack of drivers.

One thing F1 could do is to allow teams to bring three assembled cars to each Grand Prix, after all, they do bring a third car in spares, but it isn’t completely assembled. If they did that, then they could run three cars in an extended 90-minute FP1 session at all race weekends - to reduce the traffic at some events, only allow two cars from each team on the track at any one point in time.

For sprint weekends, go back to two cars for sprint qualifying and the sprint race, but legislate that each team must alternate their resident driver and run at least one driver that has never competed in more than two grand prixs.

Sprint points from both drivers competing only count towards the teams' separate ‘sprint constructors' championship’ and a ‘sprint drivers' championship’ that might just open the door to finding the next superstar.
Then after the sprint race on the Saturday your normal two grand prix drivers take over for a 30-minute FP2 session just before grand prix qualifying, with the grand prix as normal on Sunday.
Given Ocon's F1 career was such an improbability in the first place, I wouldn't rule out the prospect of him fighting his way back onto the F1 grid (again).
He's only 30, and he's currently performing at a higher level than any axed driver since probably ex-team-mate Sergio Perez's startling end to 2020.

Think of Yuki Tsunoda (Red Bull), Perez (Red Bull), Daniel Ricciardo (AlphaTauri), Kevin Magnussen (Haas), Valtteri Bottas and Zhou Guanyu (Sauber). None of them was performing anywhere near the level Ocon has managed in recent rounds.
So Ocon has the powerful weapon of incumbency for eight more rounds, driving an upgraded Haas car that now looks capable of fighting for points at most tracks.

If he can continue to deliver some Bearman-beating weekends, then he'll walk out of F1 having delivered a strong reminder that he should be the experienced driver of choice if an F1 team needs one, be it as a stand-in or full-time driver.
A return won't happen in 2027, but perhaps it will be just enough to keep him floating on the market for 2028.
keyPointsZh: 本·安德森认为奥孔不属于当前22位车手中最差的，但可能排不进前15名，面对后辈压力时位置脆弱。
哈斯仍低于成本上限运作且资金不足，付给奥孔的薪水需要更高水平的表现来支撑。
奥利·比尔曼速度太快，而F2积分领先者卡马拉带来法拉利和巴西的资金支持，在测试（TPC testing）中速度惊人。
keyPointsEn: Ben Anderson says Ocon is not the worst of the current 22 F1 drivers but is probably outside the top 15, leaving him vulnerable to pressure from below.
Haas still operates below the cost cap and is underfunded, so Ocon's salary needed to be justified by a higher level of performance.
Ollie Bearman has been too fast, and F2 points leader Rafael Camara brings Ferrari support plus Brazilian financial backing and impressed with his pace in TPC testing.

items.titleZh: 奥孔确认2026赛季末离开哈斯车队
items.summaryZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔确认将在2026赛季结束后离开哈斯F1车队，法拉利F2积分榜领跑者拉斐尔·卡马拉预计将接替他的位置。
items.originalTitle: Ocon set for F1 exit as Haas split announced
items.summaryEn: Esteban Ocon has confirmed he will leave the Haas Formula 1 team at the end of the 2026 season, with Ferrari's F2 points leader Rafael Camara set to replace him.
detailZh: 埃斯特班·奥孔已确认将在2026赛季结束时离开哈斯F1车队，法拉利F2积分榜领跑者拉斐尔·卡马拉预计将接替他。
奥孔在效力雷诺/阿尔派五个赛季后，于2025年与哈斯签下两年合同，但未能交出预期的成绩。
去年冬天，哈斯领队小松礼雄甚至承认他对奥孔2025年的表现“期待更多”，与此同时新秀队友奥利·比尔曼在下半年确立了自己作为哈斯更强车手的地位。
2026年的情况没有足够改善，未能说服哈斯在现有合同到期后继续留下奥孔。
该车手一直在测试车手以取代他，这是其旧车测试计划的一部分，该计划允许车队在私人测试中使用一辆2025年的哈斯赛车。
这些车手包括卡马拉、迈凯伦储备车手莱昂纳多·福尔纳罗利、丰田的平川亮以及前阿尔派车手杰克·杜汉。
最终，哈斯决定放弃奥孔，卡马拉极有可能取代他。
奥孔在马来西亚的巴林大奖赛前的周三确认了自己离开车队。
“我在哈斯车队（哈斯 F1 Team）的时光将在2026赛季结束后画上句号。”奥孔写道。
“我离开这个项目时问心无愧，并为自己在各种原因和因素并非总在我掌控之下的不利情况下所取得的表现感到自豪。”
“我目前的首要任务是下一个比赛周末。我将继续与车队努力合作，抓住每一个机会，并持续从赛车中榨取每一分性能。本赛季还有很多场比赛要跑，一如既往，我会为了自己、也为了车队在方向盘后拼尽全力。”
“我依然充满动力，我依然渴望胜利。这绝对不是我一级方程式职业生涯的终点。”
奥孔所说的那些情况，很可能指的是哈斯车队在零部件不一致性方面的困扰，这使得车队在整个赛季的大部分时间里都难以让两辆赛车都达到最佳状态，奥孔和贝尔曼在不同的比赛周末都受到了影响。
哈斯车队发布了官方声明，感谢奥孔为车队做出的贡献，小松礼雄表示：“我要感谢埃斯特万自2025年加入车队以来为车队做出的一切贡献。
他的职业精神和奉献精神对我们作为一支不断成长的车队来说非常宝贵。今年我们一起应对了重大规则改革的挑战，在整个赛季努力研发VF-26的过程中，埃斯特万的驾驶经验和意见发挥了重要作用。
赛季还剩下很多场比赛，我们的重点仍然是共同努力，抓住每一个机会，直到本赛季最后一场比赛结束。”
奥康目前在车手积分榜上排名第16，他在巴库带领哈斯取得了本赛季首次双人积分完赛。
随着阿斯顿·马丁确认阿隆索和斯特罗尔将继续效力至2027年，奥康在2027年将没有任何正式比赛席位的可选，因为目前只剩下梅赛德斯和小红牛（小红牛）还未确认车手阵容，而奥康对这两个席位都没有竞争力。
据The Race了解，奥康很可能在2027年寻求一个一级方程式（F1）储备车手的角色，目标是争取在2028年重返发车区。
他在2019年曾经做到过这一点，当时他在赛点车队（Racing Point）被斯特罗尔取代后被迫退居幕后，随后通过在梅赛德斯担任储备车手，一年后与雷诺车队重返一级方程式。
奥孔在2016赛季中途代表马诺车队完成了他的F1首秀，他曾在2014年击败马克斯·维斯塔潘夺得F3（三级方程式）冠军，并在一年后赢得了GP3（如今的F3）锦标赛冠军。
detailEn: Esteban Ocon has confirmed he’ll exit the Haas Formula 1 team at the end of the 2026 season, with Ferrari’s F2 points leader Rafael Camara set to replace him.
Ocon signed a two-year deal with Haas in 2025 after five seasons with Renault/Alpine, but it hasn’t delivered the expected results.

Last winter, Haas team boss Ayao Komatsu even admitted he “expected more” from Ocon in 2025, as rookie team-mate Ollie Bearman established himself as the stronger Haas driver in the second half of the year.
Things haven’t improved enough in 2026 to convince Haas to keep Ocon beyond the end of his current deal.
The team has been testing drivers to replace him as part of its Testing of Previous Cars programme, which lets it use a 2025 Haas in private tests.
Those drivers include Camara, McLaren reserve driver Leonardo Fornaroli, Toyota’s Ryo Hirakawa and ex-Alpine F1 driver Jack Doohan.
Ultimately, Haas decided to drop Ocon, with Camara highly likely to replace him.
Ocon confirmed his own exit from the team on the Wednesday before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
"My time with Haas F1 Team will come to an end at the end of the 2026 season," Ocon wrote.
"I leave this project with my head held high and proud of my performances in what were not always the easiest of circumstances for various reasons and factors outside of my control.

"My immediate focus is the next race weekend. I will continue to work hard with the team, maximise every opportunity, and keep extracting every bit of performance from the car. There are still many races to go this season and, as always, I will give it my everything behind the wheel for myself and for my team.
"I am still motivated. I am still hungry. This is absolutely not the end of my Formula 1 career."

The circumstances Ocon refers to are likely Haas's struggles with inconsistent parts that have left it struggling to run two cars optimally for a lot of the season, with both Ocon and Bearman affected on different weekends.
Haas released its own statement thanking Ocon for his services, with Komatsu saying "“I’d like to thank Esteban for everything he’s contributed to the team since joining us in 2025.

"His professionalism and commitment have proved valuable as we continue to grow as an organisation. Together this year we tackled the challenge of a major regulation change, where Esteban’s driving experience and inputs were significant as we’ve worked hard to develop the VF-26 across the season.
"There’s still plenty of racing ahead, and our focus remains on working together to maximise every opportunity through to the final race of the year.”
Ocon is currently 16th in the drivers’ championship, having led Haas’s first double points finish of the season in Baku.

With Aston Martin confirming Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll for 2027, it leaves Ocon with no race seat options for 2027, as only Mercedes and Racing Bulls haven’t confirmed their line-ups, and Ocon is a contender for neither.
The Race understands Ocon will most likely look for an F1 reserve role in 2027, with the aim of fighting back onto the grid for 2028.
He managed to do that in 2019 when he was left on the sidelines after being replaced by Lance Stroll at Racing Point, returning to F1 with Renault one year later via a reserve role with Mercedes.
Ocon made his F1 debut partway through the 2016 season for Manor, having beaten Max Verstappen to the Formula 3 title in 2014 and won the GP3 (now Formula 3) championship one year later.
keyPointsZh: 奥孔在2025年与哈斯签下两年合同，此前曾效力雷诺/阿尔派五个赛季，但成绩未达预期。
去年冬天，哈斯领队小松礼雄曾承认对奥孔2025年的表现“期待更多”，新秀队友奥利·比尔曼在下半年确立了更强的地位。
哈斯通过旧车测试计划考察了卡马拉、法纳罗利、平川亮和多汉等多位车手，最终决定放弃奥孔。

detailZh: 塞恩斯如何从F1生涯最艰难的时刻重回正轨
威廉姆斯车手在阿塞拜疆大奖赛周末开始时接受了Motorsport.com的采访
对塞恩斯来说，巴库永远不会只是一个普通的比赛地。上周在2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛前夕接受我们采访时，这位西班牙车手刚刚抵达这座城市，思绪不可避免地回到了12个月前——当时他在威廉姆斯首次登上领奖台。
这仍然是他认为自己职业生涯最佳时刻之一，但2026年的塞恩斯是在经历了几个月的困难之后来到巴库的，在此期间FW48赛车未能让他取得期望的成绩。
然而，从个人的角度来看，他的感受几乎完全相反：32岁的他觉得自己正处于职业生涯的巅峰附近，驾驶水平非常高。正是这种反差——他在方向盘后的自我感觉与成绩上的匮乏之间的矛盾——让这段时期格外令人沮丧。
MS：卡洛斯，你好吗？
卡洛斯·塞恩斯：“我很好。我昨天抵达这里准备比赛周末。这个地方让我回忆起去年的许多美好时光，那是我与威廉姆斯车队的第一个领奖台。那可能是我职业生涯中最美好的时刻之一，所以巴库现在对我而言是一个重要的地方。”
现在这个时刻，在你的生活和职业生涯中是怎样的一个时刻？
“这是一个特殊的时刻，因为就我个人的表现而言，我觉得自己度过了不错的一年。我今年32岁，我认为自己正处于职业生涯的巅峰附近。我感觉自己今年开得相当不错，但与此同时，这个赛季一直非常令人沮丧，赛车出现了很多问题，使我们无法取得好成绩。
“在某种程度上，我觉得这正在变成我职业生涯中有点荒废的一年，因为我们没能达到我们为自己设定的目标。我希望这只是一个奇怪的年份，希望下个赛季我们能发现自己处于更好的位置。”
你于2025年加入威廉姆斯，但在那之前你曾效力于小红牛、雷诺、迈凯伦和法拉利。你认为你为这支车队带来了什么？自从你来到这里之后，威廉姆斯发生了多大的变化？
“首先，我带来了我的经验以及作为一名车手速度。在一级方程式度过12年之后，我想差不多每个人都知道我的优势是什么。但最重要的是，我认为我带来了经验和一种特定的工作方式，努力帮助这支车队进步。
“我有机会体验过像法拉利这样的顶级车队，所以我可以给威廉姆斯一个参照，让他们知道一支顶级车队如今是什么水平，以及要达到那个水平还需要什么。
“好的一面是，我们还有詹姆斯·沃尔斯，他来自梅赛德斯，还有亚历克斯（阿尔本），他经历过红牛的环境。车队内部有三四个重要人物，他们都知道一支顶级车队是如何运作的。我们正在努力让威廉姆斯在未来回到那个水平。”
你已经决定把自己的未来托付给威廉姆斯。除了技术层面的原因之外，你在这支车队的成员身上看到了什么，让你愿意继续相信这个项目？
“主要有两个原因。第一是我信任这个项目、这些人以及车队的中长期愿景。诚然，今年非常令人失望，是一个谁都没有预料到的赛季。它也让我们看到我们还有多少需要改进的地方，而且我们距离目标可能比我们想象的还要远。
“去年情况几乎相反：我们取得了比预期还要好的成绩。而今年则困难得多。第二个原因是，从我到达的第一刻起就感到宾至如归。在威廉姆斯，我感觉到人们真正在倾听我，对于一名车手来说这是最根本的。我希望当我说的时候，人们会听，而且某些事情能够朝我建议的方向推进。
“到目前为止，这里正是这样。我职业生涯中最好的几个年头是在迈凯伦度过的，在法拉利的一些岁月也是如此。比如在迈凯伦，我当时的感受与现在在威廉姆斯的感受非常相似。我认为，当车手身处那样的环境时，才能发挥出最佳水平。”
你常常把自己形容为一个非常理性的人。但是否也有一个卡洛斯·塞恩斯，很难把赛道上的糟糕一天抛在脑后？
“当然有。当某一天事情不顺利时，我是那个上床睡觉时还会为所犯的错误而痛苦的人。但经验给了我很重要的一点：明白世界并不会就此终结。我们都有过好的周末和坏的周末。生活继续向前，一名车手的价值不会因为一场糟糕的比赛就突然下降。
“随着经验的积累，你学会如何在心理上应对这些情况。你知道那只是一场比赛，也许下一站在巴库你就登上领奖台，所有人都会忘记之前发生的事，突然之间你又被看作一个不同的车手。在这方面，经验的作用非常大。”
你职业生涯中最艰难的时刻是什么？
“毫无疑问是在得知我将离开法拉利之后的那几个月。说实话，我以为自己会在那里待很长时间。我们一起度过了美好的四年，我认为夏尔（勒克莱尔）和我合作得很好，车队也在朝着正确的方向前进。
“我从未想过会离开法拉利，但那种情况还是发生了，我需要两三个月的时间重新找回自己，弄清楚我想如何继续自己的职业生涯，以及我的下一个目标是什么。
“那几个月很艰难，但我想正是因为那段艰难，我后来才找到了职业生涯的最佳状态。我在澳大利亚赢了，登上了领奖台，我觉得我的2024赛季非常强劲。”
那么最好的时刻是什么呢？
“我在迈凯伦的岁月里有很多美好的回忆。我非常享受为那支车队效力，并在那里第一次登上领奖台。
“然后还有在法拉利的那些胜利。很难形容车手赢得职业生涯头几场比赛时的感受。而且我认为那四场胜利到来的方式，让每一场都变得特别。
“然后就是和威廉姆斯车队一起登上领奖台的经历。我当初选择这支车队是一次冒险，也许有些人觉得我疯了。后来我们在赛季末段拿下了三次领奖台，一切似乎都在朝着完美的方向发展。
“这正是为什么今年的情况让人难以理解。这是一个非常复杂的赛季。
你在赛车运动中背负着一个非常重要的姓氏。有没有那么一段时间，身为塞恩斯家族的一员更像是一种负担而不是一种荣耀？
“是的，尤其是在我参加卡丁车赛的最初几年。那时候，我感觉这个姓氏带给我的压力要大于它能带来的好处。小时候，我深切地感受到这种压力。我能看到，也能感觉到，因为我父亲的缘故，别人对待我的方式不一样。
“有过一些非常艰难的情况，我现在不想谈论，但在11岁到14岁之间，我还在跑卡丁车的时候，经历过一些糟糕的时刻。也许有一天我会在一本自传里谈到它们。我确实感受到了压力，我也看到有些人对一个十二三岁的男孩表现得很恶劣。我不喜欢那样。”
如果今天你能见到15岁或16岁的塞恩斯，你会告诉他这一切都是值得的吗？在“普通”青少年的生活中，有没有什么经历是你觉得自己错过的？
“我肯定会告诉他，这一切都是值得的。我从来没有真正有过一刻去质疑自己所做的一切是否值得这些牺牲，因为我一直都很享受。
“驾驶、去参赛、去竞争——这始终是我的梦想。即使我错过了16岁的孩子可能会拥有的某些普通经历，我也从不把它看作一种牺牲。我只是觉得，我正在做自己想做的事。
“当然，也有过紧张和压力的时刻，也有过我不知道自己能否进入F1、能否真正成为一名F1车手的时刻。
“对于那个曾经怀疑自己能否有朝一日达到这个高度、甚至能否在F1中赢得分站赛的男孩，我会告诉他不要担心。他会成功的。而且他的职业生涯可能会比他想象的还要好。”
detailEn: How Carlos Sainz bounced back from the most difficult moment of his F1 career
The Williams driver spoke to Motorsport.com at the start of the Azerbaijan GP weekend

Baku can never be just another place for Carlos Sainz. When we spoke to him on the eve of the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix last week, the Spaniard had only just arrived in the city and his thoughts inevitably went back to 12 months ago, having claimed his first podium with Williams.

It remains one of the moments he still considers among the best of his career, but in 2026 Sainz arrived in Baku after a difficult few months, during which the FW48 has not allowed him to achieve the results he had hoped for.

And yet, from a personal point of view, his perception is almost the opposite: at 32, he feels he is close to the peak of his career and driving at a very high level. It is precisely this contrast, between how he feels behind the wheel and the lack of results, that has made this period particularly frustrating.
MS: Carlos, how are you?

Carlos Sainz: “I’m good. I arrived yesterday for the race weekend. It’s a place that brings back a lot of great memories from last year, from my first podium with Williams. It was probably one of the best moments of my career, so Baku is now an important place for me.”
What kind of moment is this in your life and in your career?

“It’s a particular moment because, in terms of my own performance, I feel like I’m having a good year. I’m 32 and I think I’m close to the peak of my career. I feel like I’m driving quite well this year, but at the same time it has been a very frustrating season, with a lot of problems with the car that have prevented us from achieving good results.

“In a way, I feel like it is becoming a bit of a lost year in my career because we are not managing to reach the targets we had set ourselves. I hope it can simply be a strange year and that next season we can find ourselves in a better position.”

You joined Williams in 2025, but before that you raced for Toro Rosso, Renault, McLaren and Ferrari. What do you think you have brought to this team, and how much has Williams changed since you arrived?

“First of all, I brought my experience and my speed as a driver. After 12 years in Formula 1, I think more or less everyone knows what my strengths are. But above all, I think I have brought experience and a certain way of working, trying to help this team improve.
“I have had the chance to experience top teams such as Ferrari, so I can give Williams a reference for where a top team is today and what is needed to reach that level.

“The positive thing is that we also have James Vowles, who comes from Mercedes, and Alex [Albon], who has experienced the Red Bull environment. There are three or four important figures within the team who know how a top team works. We are trying to bring Williams back to that level in the future.”
You have decided to commit your future to Williams. Beyond the technical reasons, what have you seen in the people within this team that convinced you to keep believing in the project?

“There are two main reasons. The first is that I trust the project, the people and the medium- to long-term vision within the team. It is true that this year has been very disappointing, a season nobody expected. It has also shown us how much we still need to improve and that we are probably further away than we thought.

“Last year it was almost the opposite: we achieved results that were even better than expected. This year, instead, has been much more difficult. The second reason is that I have felt at home from the very first moment I arrived. At Williams, I have felt that people really listen to me, and for me as a driver that is fundamental. I want to feel that when I speak, people listen and that certain things can move in the direction I suggest.

“So far, that is exactly what has happened here. Some of the best years of my career were at McLaren, and also some of my years at Ferrari. At McLaren, for example, I felt in a very similar way to how I feel now at Williams. And I think a driver is able to perform at his best when he finds himself in that kind of environment.”
You have often described yourself as a very rational person. But is there also a Carlos Sainz who struggles to leave a bad day at the track behind him?

“Definitely. I’m the first one who, when I go to bed after a day in which things have not gone well, suffers thinking about the mistakes that were made. But experience has given me something very important: the understanding that the world does not end there. We have all had good weekends and bad weekends. Life goes on, and a driver’s value does not suddenly decrease because of one bad race.

“With experience, you learn how to manage those situations mentally. You know it is only one race, and maybe at the next one you finish on the podium in Baku, everyone forgets what happened before and suddenly you are seen as a different driver. Experience helps massively in that respect.”
What has been the most difficult moment of your career?

“Definitely the months after finding out that I would be leaving Ferrari. Honestly, I thought I was going to stay there for a long time. We had come through four good years in which I think Charles [Leclerc] and I had done a good job together, and the team was moving in the right direction.

“I never expected to leave Ferrari, but that situation happened and I needed two or three months to find myself again, understand how I wanted to continue my career and what my next objective would be.

“They were difficult months, but I think it was precisely because of that difficulty that I probably found the best form of my career afterwards. I won in Australia, achieved podiums and I think I had a very strong 2024 season.”
And what has been the best moment?
“I have so many great memories from my years at McLaren. I really enjoyed driving for that team and achieving my first podiums there.

"Then there were the wins with Ferrari. It is impossible to describe what a driver feels when he wins the first races of his career. And I think the way those four victories came makes every one of them special.

“Then there was the podium with Williams. I had taken my gamble by choosing this team and maybe some people thought I was crazy. Then we achieved three podiums towards the end of the season and everything seemed to be moving in the perfect direction.
“That is exactly why this year has been difficult to understand. It has been a really complicated season.”
You carry a very important surname in motorsport. Was there ever a time when being a Sainz felt more like a burden than a privilege?

“Yes, definitely during my first years in karting. At that time, I felt that the weight of my surname was greater than the advantages it could bring me. When I was young, I felt that pressure a lot. I could see it and I could feel that I was not being treated in the same way because of who my father was.

“There were some very difficult situations that I don’t want to talk about now, but between the ages of 11 and 14, while I was karting, I went through some bad moments. Maybe one day I will talk about them in a biography. I definitely felt the pressure, and I saw some people behave badly towards a 12- or 13-year-old boy. I did not like that.”
If you could meet the 15- or 16-year-old Carlos today, would you tell him it was all worth it? Is there anything from the life of a ‘normal’ teenager that you feel you missed out on?
“I would definitely tell him that it was worth it. I never really had a moment in which I questioned whether everything I was doing was worth the sacrifice, because I always enjoyed it.

“Driving, going to races, competing — it was always my dream. Even when I missed out on some of the normal experiences a 16-year-old might have, I never saw it as a sacrifice. I simply thought I was doing what I wanted to do.
“Of course, there were moments of tension and pressure, moments when I didn’t know whether I would make it to Formula 1 or whether I would really become a Formula 1 driver.

“To that boy who had doubts about whether he would one day make it here, or even win races in Formula 1, I would tell him not to worry. He will make it. And he will probably have an even better career than he ever imagined.”
keyPointsZh: 塞恩斯仍把去年的巴库领奖台视为其职业生涯最佳时刻之一。
keyPointsEn: Sainz still considers last year's Baku podium one of the best moments of his career.
